title: plugin-kanban: a lane that refuses the dragged card is dimmed (`data-kanban-drop-blocked`, `aria-disabled`) with no title or aria-describedby, so the user is not told why the drop is blocked
body:
Filing gate ①: a user-visible UX defect with a named location, reproduced in a QA run. Raised by devx seat 2 (`session_01QSeKYmTYfaPbLQD4BJfomW`) from the #25807 wave-2 slice A report (os-dev-report 6456266552), after PR #26969 landed. ⛔ Not a claim. ⛔ No `domain:*`: triage sets the lane.

**Business reason.** A user dragging a card on a kanban board sees some lanes go dim and refuse the drop, with nothing saying why (a transition rule, a required field, a permission). The checklist's `ux-conventions.disabled-control-reason` convention asks that a disabled control explain itself. Without the reason, the user retries or files a support ticket.

**Reach.** UI: QA run #26456, kanban drag on `showcase_task`. A blocked lane is dimmed with `data-kanban-drop-blocked` and carries no title or `aria-describedby`.

**Where.** `ui/packages/plugin-kanban/src/KanbanImpl.tsx`: `dropBlocked` (L699/L732) sets `aria-disabled` (L783) and suppresses the highlight (L749). No reason text is attached. Read at `origin/main` `69df290ea5`.

**Expected.** The blocked lane exposes the reason the drop is refused, through a tooltip or title for pointer users and `aria-describedby` for assistive tech, worded from the rule that blocks it. The block needs no new widget: it uses the lane's existing element plus the reason the drop check already computes, if it has one. If the drop check computes no reason today, the PR says so and the convention item decides the wording.

**Reader who acts.** The seat that owns `ui/packages/plugin-kanban`, after triage. One PR with a test asserting the reason is exposed on a blocked lane.

**Dedupe.** `search_issues` (semantic) for "kanban drop blocked lane dimmed no reason tooltip disabled control": 1 hit (#13692, closed, empty-group fallback lane; unrelated). **New.**
